notes: Closed-loop traces from a standalone controller+pump simulator (runLoop() in generate.R, modelled on simulatePump() in tests/testthat/test-tci-api.R).  The controller sends a request every `interval` s at t = 0, 10, ..., minutes*60 INCLUSIVE (so a 30-min trace has 181 steps), each with the whole history; receivedAt = now + 0.2 s.  The simulated pump applies the commanded rate.value at now + actualLatency and appends {time, rate, units: 'mL/hr', source: 'tci'} to the history ONLY when the value differs from the rate already running (the value is first rounded to 15 significant digits, as the JSON carries it).  The TRUE state is the seven-amplitude closed-form recurrence p <- p e^{-l dt} + pinf R (1 - e^{-l dt}) (likewise e with the four effect-site eigenvalues) advanced at the rates actually run, with R = rate.value converted through the syringe (mL/hr * concentration / 60 = mass/min); a hand bolus adds pbolus*A, ebolus*A.  `trueCp`/`trueCe` are that state at `now` (before the request); `stateNow` is the server's reconstruction from the history, which should agree to rounding. `maxTrueCe` is the maximum of the true Ce sampled every 1 s (closed form within each constant-rate span) over the whole trace; `maxTrueCeAt` its time.  The fallback branch (run fallback.rate at holdUntil if no newer command) never fires in these traces because every response is accepted and actualLatency < interval; the hold started at the switch time ends exactly when the next command lands.  `finalHistory` is the history array sent with the last request. `finalStateRelativeDifference` compares the true state with the last response's state.now (a self-check, ~1e-13). Step fields: now (request), rate {value, units, ideal, limitedBy}, controller {plan, phase}, fallbackRate, timing (all fields), stateNow {cp, ce}, stateHoldUntil {cp, ce}, prediction {peakCe, peakAt, onTarget}, trueCp, trueCe, warnings, pumpSwitchesAt (now + actualLatency).
